name: Kestrel Armored Liner Coat
description:
From the outside, this is a charcoal gray longline coat in a wool-poly blend — structured, professional, unremarkable. A Tier 3 professional could wear it to a client meeting without a second glance. The interior tells a different story: a full-torso ballistic liner constructed from flexible ceramic-polymer composite panels sewn into the lining, covering the chest, back, and sides. The panels are thin enough that the coat drapes naturally. There is no visible bulk. The collar has a raised back that protects the base of the skull.

Kestrel makes protection gear for people who can't afford to look like they need protection. Investigators, journalists, fixers, mid-level corporate operatives who've made enemies — anyone who operates in environments that aren't safe but can't afford to announce that they aren't safe. The ballistic rating is NIJ Level IIIA: stops handgun rounds, fragmentation, and most knife attacks. Rifle rounds will ruin your day but you already knew that.
functionality: Integrated concealed ballistic protection rated NIJ Level IIIA. Panels cover full torso front, back, and lateral. Raised collar provides partial neck and skull-base coverage. No electronic components.
what_it_says: You've done a threat assessment of your own life and acted on it. You're not paranoid — you're prepared.
story_hooks: Someone was shot wearing this coat and survived — but they've told no one and they're pretending the meeting went fine, which means someone doesn't know they failed
Kestrel recently received a bulk order from an anonymous buyer — forty coats, all the same size — and they fulfilled it without asking questions
The ballistic panels can be removed and repurposed; someone in the Gray Zone has figured out how to cut and reassemble them into something that fits under a Tier 1 jacket

physical_description.visual_profile: A refined, understated charcoal gray longline coat with clean lines and a professional silhouette. Appears as everyday corporate wear—no visible armor, no tactical affectation. The subtle raised collar detail is the only hint of purposeful design. Drapes with natural fluidity despite concealed ballistic panels.
physical_description.fit: Tailored but not restrictive. Structured through the shoulders and torso, with enough room for layering and movement without excess fabric. The longline cut extends mid-thigh, providing coverage while maintaining a civilian profile.
physical_description.primary_material: Wool-poly blend exterior (60% wool, 40% synthetic fiber), matte finish. Interior lined with flexible ceramic-polymer composite ballistic panels in a seamless matrix.
physical_description.texture: Exterior: smooth, dense weave with subtle texture from wool content. Interior panels: slightly textured matte finish, engineered for flex without acoustic signature. Seams reinforced at stress points.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal gray exterior with slate undertones. Interior ballistic panels are muted graphite with minimal contrast. No bright accents or branding visible.
physical_description.closures: Front button closure (4 buttons, brushed steel), hidden interior magnetic snaps for quick panel access. Wrist cuffs have friction-fit closures.
distinctive_features: Raised back collar protecting cervical spine
Invisible ballistic liner extending full torso—chest, back, and side panels
NIJ Level IIIA ceramic-polymer composite construction
Hidden interior seam access for maintenance or panel replacement
Kestrel brand insignia (small woven tag inside collar only)
Reinforced interior anchor points for optional hardware
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 professional—functional protection marketed as civilian wear. Price point suggests mid-level corpo, security specialist, or established fixer. Not cheap, but not ostentatiously wealthy.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by people who live in managed danger: corporate investigators, freelance journalists in contested zones, diplomatic security, fixers who handle sensitive work, mid-tier operatives. Signals quiet competence and acceptance of risk without broadcasting vulnerability.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine to broken-in. When new, the coat looks corporate-generic. Over time, subtle creases form around the panel seams (internal), minor scuffs accumulate on cuffs and lower hem, and the fabric develops a lived-in patina. Ballistic panels show no external wear.
